# MinION 
Data from a previous MinION run on a culture dominated by a bacterium in the genus Vibrio. The dominant organism has two large chromosomes with sizes around 3.4Mb and 1.8Mb respectively. We also expect some smaller plasmids. At very high coverage it was also revealed that this data contained another bacterium (a Gammaproteobacterium) which was around 100 times less abundant than the Vibrio.

# Redbean assembly
- one of the fastest long read genome assemblers

```{bash}
cd redbean
pwd

#first 3 files which equates to 12000 reads and around 6x coverage of the target genome
cat /pvol/data/amtp4/*_[012]f.fastq > amtp4.fastq

#run assembly
wtdbg2 -x ont -g 5m -t 4 -i amtp4.fastq -fo amtp4
wtpoa-cns -t 4 -i amtp4.ctg.lay.gz -fo amtp4.ctg.fa

#time taken = real 44.070 sec, user 185.530 sec, sys 8.140 sec

```

# Activity 1 
Inspect assembly statistics USING REDBEAN
```{bash}
assembly-stats amtp4.ctg.fa

#output
stats for amtp4.ctg.fa
sum = 3816931, n = 129, ave = 29588.61, largest = 159610
N50 = 48075, n = 23 # 
N60 = 33615, n = 33
N70 = 28879, n = 45
N80 = 21464, n = 60
N90 = 13023, n = 83
N100 = 2697, n = 129 #
N_count = 0
Gaps = 0

```
contiguity: n = contig size at which half of all assembles bases reside in contigs of this size or longer (Longest contig = 0) 
smallest quantitiy at top half of assembly 

completeness (closer to 1 = more ), proportion of estimated genome: assembled genome size/ estimated genome size 

## Run Redbean with higher coverage
REDO assembly with better coverage depth (number of reads in a contig)
Data equivalent to ~20x coverage
```{bash}
#run assembly
cat /pvol/data/amtp4/*.fastq > amtp4_20x.fastq
wtdbg2 -x ont -g 5m -t 4 -i amtp4_20x.fastq -fo amtp4_20x
wtpoa-cns -t 4 -i amtp4_20x.ctg.lay.gz -fo amtp4_20x.ctg.fa

#time taken:real 164.938 sec, user 603.150 sec, sys 32.890 sec
```

```{bash}
assembly-stats amtp4_20x.ctg.fa
```

# Bandage 
Depth - average number of reads that cover a given region of the genome sequence e.g., 50x or 100x coverage
- to assemble a gene : needs overlaps, long reads,account for errors
e.g., 
read 1:     xxxx
read 2:     xxxxxx
read 3: xxxxxx
contig: xxxxxxxxxx
depth = 3, contig = 1

repeat: central or around circle, other contigs "pass through"

# Activity 3
Inspect low coverage flye assembly with Bandage

## Assembly graphs with Bandage

download amtp4/assembly_graph.gfa
Load graph into Bandage  

1. Biologically distinct entities such as chromosomes or plasmids will form separate graphs
2. Separated graphs can also occur if coverage is very low and no reads exist to join parts of the assembly together
3. Highly joined regions (eg top left) tend to occur because repeats create ambiguities. There are too many connections and the assembler has trouble choosing the correct path between them.

# Activity 4
Inspect high coverage flye assembly with Bandage
download amtp4_20x/assembly_graph.gfa
Load graph into Bandage 

Can you spot the same repeat region? 
repeat region in small connected to multiple chromosomes but only connects 1 chromosome in the larger 

How has increased coverage changed the appearance of the assembly.
increased coverage clearly defined the chromosomes more
improved contiguity and completion

Which contigs look like fully assembled chromosomes? 
first 2 lines? longer assemblies

Which ones look like plasmids?
last few lines? very short assemblies

## Assembly quality with QUAST

Move to the QUAST folder
```{bash}
cd ..
cd quast
pwd
```

Prepare Flye assembly data 
```{bash}
#look at contig size in flye assembly 
cat ../flye_genome/amtp4_20x/assembly.fasta | bioawk -c fastx '{print $name, length($seq)}' | sort -n -k2
```
2 largest contigs: 
contig_3        1775265
contig_15       3378256

```{bash}
#extract 2 largest contigs from assembly
samtools faidx ../flye_genome/amtp4_20x/assembly.fasta contig_3 contig_15 > flye_asm/vibrio.fasta
```

Prepare Redbean assembly
```{bash}
#look at contig size in flye assembly 
cat ../redbean/amtp4_20x.ctg.fa | bioawk -c fastx '{print $name, length($seq)}' | sort -n -k2

```
2 largest contigs: 
ctg2    1764934
ctg1    3342848

```{bash}
#extract 2 largest contigs from assembly
samtools faidx ../redbean/amtp4_20x.ctg.fa ctg2 ctg1 > redbean_asm/vibrio.fasta
```

Create a symbolic link to the original reads
```{bash}
ln -s ../flye_genome/amtp4_20x.fastq .
ln -s /pvol/data/amtp4/reference/vibrio .
```

Run QUAST
```{bash}
quast -o quast_vibrio redbean_asm/vibrio.fasta flye_asm/vibrio.fasta -L -t 4 --circos --glimmer -r vibrio/vibrio.fna --features  vibrio/vibrio.gff --nanopore amtp4_20x.fastq
```
# Activity 5 
Inspect quast outputs
 1 Main report.html
 2. circos plot in circos/circos.png
 
Both assemblers seem to have done a very good job of assembling the genome but both have produced regions where there are a large number of small differences (snps and indels) between the assembly and the reference. The redbean assembly also seems to have a couple of gaps which most likely correspond with the highly repetitive region we observed in the Bandage visualisation.
